small_guidance:
- The autotune space declares `BLOCK_N`/`BLOCK_K` but the launcher hard-codes `BLOCK_M=64` outside the configs — promote `BLOCK_M` into the autotune configs (try 32/64/128) so the OC tile can be co-tuned with `BLOCK_N`; with OC=64, a single `BLOCK_M=64` program covers all channels and frees the grid for larger spatial tiles.
- Hoist the per-`(kd,kh,kw)` weight gather: load the full `(BLOCK_M, IC)` weight slab once per `(kd,kh,kw)` (or once per kh,kw with a kd inner loop) and reuse it across the spatial tile; currently the w load is inside the IC loop and re-reads identical weights. Equivalently, swap loop order so IC is the outermost K-accumulation and (kd,kh,kw) are static — this turns the GEMM-K dim into `IC*KD*KH*KW=864` which `tl.dot` can chew through with fewer redundant loads.
- Add larger `BLOCK_N` configs (256, 512) with `num_warps=8`, `num_stages=3`, and consider `BLOCK_K=16` since IC=32 means BLOCK_K=32 already covers the channel dim in one shot — a smaller BLOCK_K only helps if IC grows.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM with K = `IC*KD*KH*KW` (=864) as the contraction axis and N = `OD*OH*OW` (=120000) as the spatial axis: one program computes a `(BLOCK_M_oc, BLOCK_N_spatial)` output tile and iterates K in `BLOCK_K` chunks, computing `(ic, kd, kh, kw)` from the flat k index. This lets `tl.dot` run on a true GEMM shape and eliminates the triple-nested static loop with redundant weight loads.
- Switch the output (and input) to channels-last (`NDHWC`) so the spatial axis is the contiguous one for the store and for the input gather along the K dim — this fixes the current strided per-channel loads/stores which are killing bandwidth on a 16×64×30×62×62 tensor.
- Fuse bias + Mish + Tanh in the epilogue (already done) but also persist the program across the batch dim (`pid_b` loop inside the kernel) so the weight tile, once loaded, is reused across all N batches — weight reuse is the biggest single win since W is only 64·32·27·4 B = 221 KB and fits comfortably in L2.
